newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Procter Brazil sees revs rising with new brands.
newsitem.headline: Procter Brazil sees revs rising with new brands.

text.p: Procter & Gamble's Brazilian unit said it expects to increase its annual revenues by 30 percent after the acquisition of three laundry detergent brands and two plants from Brazil's Bombril SA.

The company, which had annual revenues of $400 million in 1995, agreed to buy Bombril's ODD Fases, Quanto and Pop powder laundry detergents and two manufacturing plants -- one in Sao Paulo and one in Salvador, northeastern Brazil.
It also acquired Finish automatic dishwashing powder detergent.
The purchase was announced last Friday and marked Procter & Gamble's debut in the powder detergent market in Brazil, the group's second market in Latin America after Mexico.
"This acquisition was very important under our growth plans in Brazil," said Richard Laube, president of Procter & Gamble do Brasil.
Exact financial terms of the deal were not disclosed, but Laube said the transaction was around $100 million.

Laube said that, after these acquisitions, the company will be able to achieve its target of reaching $1 billion in revenues by the year 2000. The company has no plans to make new purchases, he added.
He also said the firm will invest $60 million in 1997, including on advertising.

The new brands acquired by Procter & Gamble do Brasil account for between 16 percent and 17 percent of the Brazilian powder detergent market, which is worth $700-$800 million, said financial director Winston Griffin.
Procter & Gamble had sales of $35.3 billion worldwide in the fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, with about six percent of those sales coming from Latin America.
It offers more than 300 brands in 140 countries. These brands include Tide, Ariel, Pantene Pro-V and Pringles.
